courses.description:
This is a hands-on course on how modern web applications break, and how to fix them. It is built from the
*Modern Web Application Development and Exploitation* course I assessed as Exam Architect at Amrita,
including the 7-scenario CTF used as its end-semester exam.

Every lesson follows the same loop: **understand** the mechanism, **exploit** it in a safe lab,
then **fix** it in code. Nothing here should ever be pointed at a system you don't own or have
written permission to test.
outcomes: Read and craft raw HTTP requests, and explain how state is kept with cookies and sessions
Intercept, modify and replay traffic with browser DevTools and Burp Suite
Find, exploit and fix SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, path traversal and IDOR in a lab
Write clear, reproducible vulnerability reports with a fix for each finding
Solve a multi-stage web CTF end to end
prerequisites: Basic HTML and JavaScript (you can read a simple web page's source)
Comfortable on a Linux command line
A laptop that can run Docker for the lab machines

modules.title: Foundations of the web
modules.summary: How browsers and servers really talk, and the tools we'll use to watch them do it.

lessons.title: How the web talks: HTTP
lessons.summary: Every web attack starts with a request. Learn to read and write HTTP by hand.
objectives: Describe the structure of an HTTP request and response
Explain what methods, status codes and headers are for
Send raw requests with curl and read the full response

lessons.title: Cookies & sessions
lessons.summary: HTTP forgets you after every request. Cookies are how the web remembers, and how attackers impersonate you.
objectives: Explain how session cookies turn stateless HTTP into a logged-in experience
Read and evaluate cookie attributes (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Path, Expires)
Spot common session-handling mistakes in a lab application

lessons.title: SQL injection: the basics
lessons.summary: When user input is pasted into a database query, the user gets to write part of your SQL.
objectives: Explain why string-built SQL queries are injectable
Confirm and exploit a basic SQL injection in a lab login form
Fix the bug with parameterized queries, and explain why escaping alone isn't enough

modules.title: Client-side attacks
modules.summary: Attacks that run in the victim's browser.

modules.title: Server-side & access control
modules.summary: Reading files you shouldn't, and seeing data that isn't yours.
